issues.legal_issue: An amendment to a written statement may add a conditional qualification to an admission and raise a defence about a claimant’s entitlement without impermissibly withdrawing the admission or displacing the claimant’s case.
material_facts: The defendants had admitted that the plaintiff and certain other defendants were entitled to a half share in the properties.
The proposed amendment retained that admission but added a qualification that entitlement depended on proving the relevant claimants’ legitimacy and right to inherit.
The amendment raised an issue for determination and did not replace the plaintiff’s case or cause irretrievable prejudice.
The trial had not commenced when the amendment was sought.
issues.conclusion: The amendment was permissible, and the application to amend the written statement was allowed.
issues.legal_principle: Under Order VI Rule 17 of the Code of Civil Procedure, pleadings may be amended where necessary to determine the real controversy; the post-commencement due-diligence proviso did not apply because the trial had not commenced. Courts generally take a more liberal approach to amendments of written statements than amendments of plaints: a defendant may add or alter a defence, take inconsistent pleas, and explain an admission, provided the amendment does not cause serious injustice or irreparable prejudice. The Court relied on Ma Shwe Mya v. Maung Mo Hnaung, B.K. Narayana Pillai v. Parameswaran Pillai, Baldev Singh v. Manohar Singh, L.J. Leach and Co. Ltd. v. Jardine Skinner and Co., Basavan Jaggu Dhobi v. Sukhnandan Ramdas Chaudhary, and Akshaya Restaurant v. P. Anjanappa. It distinguished Modi Spinning & Weaving Mills Co. Ltd. v. Ladha Ram & Co. and Heera Lal v. Kalyan Mal because the proposed amendment here preserved the admission and did not displace the claimant’s case or cause irretrievable prejudice.

rule.if: civil_written_statement_amendment_case and admission_preserved_with_qualification and amendment_raises_issue_for_decision and not irretrievable_prejudice

predicates.civil_written_statement_amendment_case: A party in a civil suit sought to amend its written statement.
predicates.admission_preserved_with_qualification: The proposed amendment retained an earlier admission while adding a qualification to it.
predicates.amendment_raises_issue_for_decision: The proposed amendment added facts or a defence relevant to resolving an issue in the dispute.
predicates.irretrievable_prejudice: The proposed amendment would cause the opposing party irretrievable prejudice.

issues.definition: When a party in a civil suit seeks to amend its written statement, retaining an admission while qualifying it to raise a relevant issue without irretrievable prejudice means the amendment is permitted.

issues.legal_issue: A supervisory court should not reverse a trial court’s discretionary decision allowing a pleading amendment when the trial court exercised its discretion on the applicable principles and the record.
material_facts: The trial court considered the written statement, the proposed amendment, and the applicable principles before allowing the amendment.
The High Court reversed that discretionary order and rejected the amendment.
The proposed amendment did not withdraw the admission or cause irretrievable prejudice.
issues.conclusion: The High Court was not justified in reversing the trial court’s discretionary order allowing the amendment.
issues.legal_principle: The Court held that the High Court should not have reversed the trial court’s discretionary order in the exercise of its supervisory jurisdiction under Article 227 of the Constitution when the trial court had exercised its discretion after considering the legal principles and the material on record.

predicates.supervisory_review_of_amendment_order_ca: A supervisory court reviewed a trial court’s discretionary order on an application to amend a pleading.
predicates.trial_court_exercised_discretion_on_prin: The trial court considered the governing principles and material on the record when deciding the amendment application.

issues.definition: In supervisory review of an amendment order, when the trial court exercised its discretion on the governing principles and the record, the supervisory court should not reverse that discretionary order.
